Hi all — quick note on what's happening and a practical workaround.

Diagnosis:
- When an .ics is forwarded by some mail clients or through Google Calendar's "Forward" action, the TZID (e.g. "Asia/Singapore") can be stripped and the event becomes "floating" — Google then renders it relative to the recipient's local TZ, which explains Anna seeing 08:30 CEST instead of 10:30 SGT.

Workarounds (pick one):
A) Send two separate invites anchored to the appropriate TZ (Asia/Singapore and Europe/Paris). This is the most reliable.
B) Keep a single invite but put the UTC timestamp and an explicit line in the event description: "This event occurs at 02:30 UTC on 2027-03-16 (10:30 SGT / 03:30 CET). Do not rely on forwarded calendar entries." Not ideal but better than nothing.
C) Use a meeting link with an absolute UTC time in the link text (we include https://calendly.com/ or the Zoom link with the UTC time) and ask attendees to RSVP rather than forward.

I'll set up two anchored invites if you want me to create them (and I can link back to the HubSpot meeting record).

Grace O'Connor
Customer Success — Redwood Inference
